  • The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
  • "Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," remarked Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.

The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.

"Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," remarked Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.

Industry observers note that "These are proven, commercial and scalable today. Now is the moment for faster implementation.".

According to recent reports, yet Australia is also the world's third-largest exporter of fossil fuels. And unlike France and Germany, or island nations from Fiji to the Bahamas that are highly vulnerable to a changing climate, the COP31 co-president has not yet committed to phasing them out.

As calls grow for the country to set a clear route to a clean energy future, critics say its vague promise to transition away from polluting sources of power does not go far enough.

Australia is home to 56% of the world's coal mine projects presently in the pipeline, notes environmental nonprofit, 350.org.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at the organization, is calling on the country, the world's second-largest coal exporter, to reverse course and announce an "overdue coal phaseout date" during the COP31 conference.

"Australia needs to walk the walk and follow Germany's example and commit to a phaseout," stated Melanie Pill, founder of The Climate Project, an Australia-based climate policy advisory.

The argument to end fossil fuel production is not only about cutting emissions but reducing dependence on energy systems that rely on volatile oil and gas markets, she explained.

"A fossil phaseout in the face of the enduring and escalating conflict in the Middle East is in the interest of everyone," Pill told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This is especially true for Australia's diesel-reliant Pacific neighbors, who spend up to 25% of GDP on fossil fuel imports — as opposed 6% on health — according to a report by the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of Newly introduced South Wales.

As lead negotiator at the UN climate talks, Australia can "flip the narrative" on a fossil fuel phaseout, using the challenge of energy security as a justification, mentioned Pill.

This opportunity could be lost, however, if Australia fails to address fossil fuel exports that accounted for 80% of its total carbon footprint in 2022 — and near 5% of global emissions.

While the nation is a world leader in rooftop solar, and generates around half of its electricity from renewables, this progress is "being undone by its continued approval of more fossil fuels for export," noted Simon Bradshaw, COP31 lead and climate expert at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

He noted that the Labor government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has approved the construction, expansion or extension of 38 coal, oil and gas projects since coming to power four years ago on a pro-climate platform.

"You cannot aspire to lead on climate abroad if you're not getting your own house in order," mentioned Thomas Houlie, climate and energy policy analyst at Climate Analytics, a global climate policy institute.

In 2025, when Australia approved the extension of a major gas export project in the country's west until 2070, Albanese justified the move in the name of a balance between "security of energy supply" and "support [for] the transition which reduces our emissions.".

It has been revealed that the country has publicly backed a global transition away from the fossil fuels driving the global temperature rise linked to extreme heat and drought. Both through the Global Stocktake agreed at the 2023 UN climate summit, and via the inaugural "transitioning away" summit in Colombia this April, at which Australia and 56 countries pledged to develop a fossil fuel exit road map.

But these commitments are not reflected in Australian resources policy, or its domestic rollout of clean power infrastructure.

"While the government has set a renewables target for electricity, it leaves plenty of blind spots in other sectors," remarked Houlie, adding that emission reductions in industry and transport have been limited and that the push to achieve an 82% renewables target for the electricity grid by 2030 is behind schedule.

In its role as lead negotiator at COP31, Australia has promised to ensure that any final conference text serves to "elevate the views and the experiences" of small Pacific nations in its region, from Vanuatu to Tuvalu.

These island countries that generate low emissions yet suffer extreme climate impacts from worsening cyclones or rising seas are "sick of Australia's double talk on climate," remarked Shiva Gounden, head of Pacific at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

It has been revealed that australia must commit to "substantial latest funding contributions" to help Pacific neighbors adapt to the climate emergency and achieve energy independence, said his colleague Bradshaw. He reiterated the need to concurrently create a "national road map" away from coal and gas production and export.

In a recent development, A Climate Analytics report co-authored by Houlie outlines a fossil fuel phaseout pathway for Australia that can begin immediately. This includes an end to coal power generation by 2034 and a rapid reduction in oil and gas consumption, with renewables generating almost all the country's electricity by 2040. Fossil fuel export projects would be eliminated, and existing ones shuttered before becoming obsolete.

"This co-presidency is a golden opportunity for Australia to step up and commit to a phaseout," noted Houlie.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of key saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

Recent findings suggest that “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

Industry observers note that “We have to change our mind swiftly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

According to recent reports, it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

It has been revealed that mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

When Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Recent findings suggest that robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

Sources indicate that “We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa mentioned. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

Industry observers note that “We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

Zion Suzuki had major gloves to fill this summer after the sale of Emiliano Martínez but already appears one of the Premier League signings of the summer.

Aston Villa’s fresh No 1 epitomises the vibrant energy of Unai Emery’s revamped squad and is a goalkeeper perfectly suited to the modern game.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. It started by accusing Carragher of “unacceptable insults to the club and its fans”, then concluded with the vainglorious declaration that “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

It has been revealed that emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard stated: “For different reasons, not only rest.”.

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, has made one change with Sander Berge replacing Hugo Larsson in midfield.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery remarked. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

In a recent development, in the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha aimed a subtle dig at Manchester United by suggesting his side should have scored more than four goals in today’s game.

Ngumoha was in superb form for Liverpool as they beat Man Utd 4-0, and it’s fair to say it was a pretty easy game for the Reds, with plenty of chances for an even bigger score-line.

Speaking after the game, the 18-year-old sounded delighted to shine in this big game, admitting that it’s special to score and assist at such a young age against Liverpool’s rivals.

Sources indicate that “Games like Liverpool-United can’t really get much bigger in my eyes. To get the three points here at Anfield is special. It was a really notable game today,” Ngumoha mentioned in his post-match interview, as quoted by BBC Sport.

In a recent development, on possibly scoring more against the Red Devils, he added: “Sometimes when we are two goals up we can get a substantial complacent really. We kept our heads in the game and started controlling it and in the second half we took the game by the scruff of the neck and revealed the mentality. We didn’t slack off.

“As fans they always want us to score chances and we know we should have scored more. Creating those chances is important as well. It’s about keeping a cool head and keeping composed and they will come.”.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim explains how he made the most of ‘brave’ Frosinone’s approach to run riot in the spaces and focus on the ‘pace’ in his Milan side for a 5-1 win. ‘The team believe in the plan.’.

It was a morale-boosting performance from the Rossoneri against a Frosinone side who changed tactics to 3-4-3 with a False 9 for this trip to San Siro.

It left massive gaps in defence that Milan took full advantage of with a counter-attacking masterclass, as after Gabriele Calvani’s own goal, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic ran riot.

The only negative was the Patrizio Masini goal to temporarily make it 2-1 going into the half-time break, while Goncalo Ramos went off with a muscular twinge.

“The main thing is that we have a initiative in the game, and the team believe in the plan,” Amorim told DAZN Italia.

According to recent reports, “You know Frosinone as well as I do, they are all about full pressure, I understood that with a lot of points coming to San Siro, they would be really brave. With the pace we have with Rabiot, Moreira, Pulisic and Ramos, we could make transitions.

“We changed a little bit the way we play the game because of our opponents, and it was a good night for us.”.

Goncalo Ramos scored his first goal since October 19, while Jashari hadn’t ever scored in the Milan jersey before this evening.

In a recent development, “We are building principles and understanding the game. We knew Frosinone are about marking man to man, that’s why Pulisic looked like he was in every position, because we knew they would follow us, and we could create a lot of danger with changing roles,” continued Amorim.

In a recent development, “It doesn’t matter who plays, every player in training needs to understand every position on the pitch, so that we can change the characteristics. There are so many things I saw in the game that we need to improve, but we stuck to the plan, and that is something I am pleased with.”.

When Ramos went off with a calf twinge, why did Amorim turn to Cisse and not Francesco Camarda?

In a recent development, “You saw the game, we did not spend many minutes around the box, the space was behind. If we were controlling the game in a different way, Camarda was the right way to play, but Cisse is really good with pace. You saw the trouble he made for the opponent was not holding the ball, it was the runs behind, the passes, not a typical striker,” explained the coach.

“I didn’t notice it was Ramos who scored the goal, it was more vital that it was 2-0, because Milan need lots of goals to control a game, and also Frosinone had to put more men forward at 2-0, so it opened up more spaces for us.”.

Milan have won five of the last six Serie A matches, and consolidated fourth place in the hunt for Champions League qualification.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time.

‘I think that performance was an improvement from where we’ve been in recent weeks.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • It has been revealed that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

It has been revealed that anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

According to recent reports, the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has released its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

The IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the firm to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company announced that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a new governance structure that it states is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of new medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei remarked in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

Industry observers note that the company has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and stated it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We plan to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Recent findings suggest that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the tech giant hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

It has been revealed that some of the company’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a new CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

In a recent development, in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

“Expectations are sky high,” indicates Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

In a recent development, but Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the tech giant was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

On 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at New York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic unveiled the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

In another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

According to recent reports, anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

#71534. Industry News: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas.
  • Recent findings suggest that if fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels.
  • Recent findings suggest that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas. Which also means significantly slashing the heat-trapping CO2 emissions that are linked to flooding and extreme heat around the world.

Recent findings suggest that if fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels. That is according to a recent analysis by the International Energy Agency, which also found that such an acceleration could mean the world needs 18 million fewer barrels of oil per day.

Recent findings suggest that in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives. That means switching from diesel cars to electric vehicles (EVs), turning off gas heating and using electricity to power heat pumps.

In a recent development, but the way the electricity running these things is generated is also important. In theory, an EV using power created in a coal-heavy electricity grid could be worse for the climate than a car running on gas.

Electricity derived from renewable energy sources such as solar, wind or hydropower on the other hand produces clean power.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The booming EV market is the fastest-growing electrification sector. Globally, one in four cars sold in 2025 was electric and since 2020, international sales have increased by almost 600%.

Nonetheless, electricity only covers about 20% of final energy use in the wider global economy, including that used in businesses, factories and people's homes.

It would need to supply more than half of all power by 2050 if we are to avoid runaway heating and the more intense and extreme weather events connected to a hotter climate.

Industry observers note that some industries and activities are harder to electrify than others. While it's relatively easy to switch to EVs and decarbonize buildings, some industries such as petrochemicals and steel use fossil fuels as raw materials to make products like plastics, fertilizer, detergent or steel.

In addition, while heat pumps work well for low-temperature needs, they can't replace the temperatures needed in steelmaking or cement production.

The World Resources Institute, an independent research organization, recommends hydrogen, synthetic fuels or other low-carbon alternatives as more viable options than electrification in cases such as ocean shipping and aviation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In addition to cutting down on greenhouse gas emissions resulting in cleaner air and limiting global heating, electrification is also more efficient and cheaper in the long run.

A combustion engine in a car wastes as much as 80% of its fuel energy, mostly to turn it into heat. Only about 20% is converted to actually move the car. Electric motors, on the other hand, convert about 80% of electrical energy into motion.

As the World Resources Institute points out, running all appliances on electricity will increase electricity consumption. Yet total energy costs are likely to be lower, even if electricity becomes more expensive.

Industry observers note that as electricity needs grow due to the rapid expansion of AI, data centers and the overall shift to a more electrified world, outpaced grids struggle to keep up. This is increasingly holding back the energy transition, delaying the rollout of additional renewable generation, storage capacity and electrified demand.

According to the International Energy Agency, annual grid investment has to increase by about 50% by 2030 from today's $400 billion.

There's also a major mismatch between how long it takes to set up newly introduced grid infrastructure (five to 15 years), compared to renewable energy projects (one to five years), and EV charging infrastructure (one to two years).

Experts say we need smarter grids that support a two-way flow of electricity while remaining secure, stable and able to keep up with higher demand as electrification intensifies.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things did not go according to proposal for Mauricio Pochettino in his first game as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss was given one of the toughest tasks of all in his first game in charge, a trip to old rivals Liverpool at Anfield and almost from the outset it was an absolute nightmare for a manager tasked with revolutionising Manchester United.

Sources indicate that eight minutes in, United were reduced to ten men, with Leny Yoro sent off for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak as he went through on goal. And then, within five minutes, United were 2-0 down with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz volleying home from a Rio Ngumoha cutback.

Ngumoha himself scored in the second half, with substitute Victor Munoz rounding off the route with a fourth late on.

The red card was the substantial talking point in the match, with questions raised as to whether it reached the threshold for the denial of a golascoring opportunity.

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber thought the right decision was made.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, he noted: "I think it was a red card.

"I think everybody in the stadium and most pundits and when I first saw it, I thought it was a red card. and I thought it was, in fact, quite an easy decision.".

The discussion has been around the four points that need to be met for it to be considered the denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, three of those considerations were clearly met, but the question is, did Isak have control of the ball when he was bearing down on goal? Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens was quick off his line and pounced on the ball soon after Iask was brought dow, leading to suggestions Isak would not have got on to his errant touch.

It has been revealed that barber disagreed. He added: "The consideration that the referee has to make, he probably has to make these decisions in a millisecond, so I think people need to understand how promptly that has to be computed through his head.

Recent findings suggest that "The distance between the offence and the goal is one of the things he has to consider. He obviously looks at the general direction of play, and then also whether there are the defenders around him or not, but the one that comes into question is the likelihood of Isak winning the ball.

Sources indicate that "Who is to say whether Isak would have got the ball or not? He was running at pace, at real pace at that time. Can you overturn a red card based on that? Highly unlikely, and that's why I don't think VAR was brought into the case because no one will ever know unless a red card was never issued, if the foul was never committed, if he would have got onto the ball.

"In that instance alone, with that particular part of the law, I think the decision was correct.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Recent findings suggest that few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta said, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

“There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

Sources indicate that the result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

In a recent development, A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

Industry observers note that referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

It has been revealed that it might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola mentioned Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

Recent findings suggest that what is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, stated.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

Industry observers note that “That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta remarked. And that was indisputable.

Industry observers note that even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

In fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

And the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

There was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

Recent findings suggest that that was the hosts’ last tangible opportunity to score. As well as Arsenal defended, it was not a good afternoon for Liverpool’s forwards, Bradley Barcola in particular, although it was interesting to see Arsenal double-up on Rio Ngumoha when he came on. Arteta reacted by bringing on a second left-back, in Piero Hincapié.

Here is a question I did not think I would be asking at any stage this season: will Liverpool win the Premier League?

It would be premature to describe this Sunday’s Anfield fixture as a title duel. Arsenal are better equipped to defend their crown, while Liverpool are a work in progress.

Whatever the outcome this weekend, Arsenal will leave Merseyside as the overwhelming favourites to claim back-to-back titles. They have a six-point lead over Liverpool. Should that extend to nine, Andoni Iraola’s primary objective coming into this season will remain unchanged; qualifying for the Champions League will represent a promising start to his reign.

What makes this weekend more significant is the champions will find a different Anfield to that which ended last season in such a downbeat mood, and came into this one uncertain of what was in store.

The discussion about what is achievable for Liverpool in the coming months is evolving by the week, the team bubbling along slightly under the radar.

There are several reasons why there are those who believe Iraola’s side might push Arsenal closer than anticipated.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool, who start the game in fifth with 15 points, and Arsenal, six points in front of them in second place. Anfield, that glorious night in May 1989 excepted, has not been the happiest of hunting grounds for Arsenal and though their record there recently – three draws in the last four visits – has perked up, they have gone 13 seasons without a victory, so long ago, in fact, that Mikel Arteta was in the side that celebrated Lukas Podolski  and Santo Cazorla earning them a 2-0 win.

Having already lost within the perimeter of the historic county of Lancashire this week, when knocked out of the Carabao Cup on penalties by League Two Fleetwood Town, the champions will be keen to end that barren streak and go into the 4.30pm kick-off on the back of three successive league victories following their defeat by Brighton. Points today, one or three, will put them ahead of Manchester City at the top of the table while victory for Liverpool would allow them to overtake Chelsea and move one point behind Brighton, the team they beat last week with the kind of performance that inspired talk of a credible title campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are considering a January move for Ivan Toney as Mauricio Pochettino looks to add a proven Premier League goalscorer to his attacking options.

The 30-year-old has been in outstanding form for Al-Ahli and is now weighing up a return to England.

United are among several Premier League clubs who have been contacted about his availability, but the prospect of moving to Old Trafford is understood to appeal strongly to the England international.

According to TEAMtalk, intermediaries are actively exploring a January return to the Premier League for Toney, with Man United among the clubs being kept informed.

Toney has scored 16 goals in 15 starts this season and still has 18 months remaining on his Al-Ahli contract.

A loan deal with an option to buy is right now being explored, which could make the transfer more realistic for United.

Pochettino has made signing a centre-forward one of his priorities, and Toney’s Premier League experience makes him attractive because he would require very little adaptation.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham have also been informed of his situation, while Crystal Palace are interested in reuniting him with former Brentford manager Thomas Frank.

The logic behind this move is strong.

It has been revealed that united need goals immediately rather than another young striker requiring time to develop. Toney already knows the league, can play with his back to goal and offers a reliable penalty-box presence.

A recent CaughtOffside report also revealed that United have been exploring a temporary deal rather than committing to a permanent transfer straight away.

Benjamin Šeško remains part of United’s long-term plans, so spending heavily on another young No.9 could create unnecessary competition once he returns to full fitness.

Toney would offer something different: experience, physicality and immediate Premier League pedigree.

The biggest question is whether Al-Ahli are prepared to sanction a loan.

Recent findings suggest that if they are, United should move swiftly. A short-term deal would limit financial risk while giving Pochettino a striker capable of making an immediate impact.

For a side struggling for consistency in attack, Toney looks like one of the most practical January options available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Playing for Barcelona, particularly during an era when Lionel Messi spearheaded an attack that also featured Luis Suarez and Neymar, is about as good as it gets for a footballer's career.

Yet, one star who was part of that squad between 2015 and 2020 saw his career completely spiral off course during his time in Catalonia, and is now nowhere near as revered as his Champions League, La Liga and Ballon d'Or-winning counterparts.

The player in question was once considered a wonderkid at Galatasaray, with many fans drawing comparisons between his playing style and that of the great Luis Figo.

A winger and number 10 hybrid who didn't rely on raw pace, but instead used his exceptional ball control and footballing intelligence to become an elite dribbler, he was a rare breed. However, being surrounded by greatness doesn't necessarily mean it will rub off on you.

Having become one of Diego Simeone's most trusted lieutenants following his move from Galatasaray early in his career, 100-cap Turkish international Arda Turan saw his career go up in flames following a big-money move to Barcelona in 2015.

It has been revealed that fresh off the back of a historic treble the previous season, Turan was expected to be the perfect attacking midfielder to slot in behind the iconic MSN frontline. However, due to the club's ongoing transfer ban, Barcelona were unable to register him immediately. Consequently, he didn't make his debut until January 6, 2016 - almost six months after arriving - meaning he was playing catch-up from the get-go.

According to recent reports, unsurprisingly, he struggled to find his feet, and talk of a potential exit emerged towards the end of the season. Luis Enrique, who had personally pushed for his signing, was nevertheless keen to persevere with the midfielder.

In a recent development, turan even became the sixth player in Barcelona's history to score a Champions League hat-trick in December 2016, before bagging another treble later that month in a Copa del Rey thrashing of Hercules. However, what appeared to be a turning point ultimately proved to be a false dawn.

In a recent development, as soon as Enrique departed and Ernesto Valverde took charge ahead of the 2017/18 season, Turan's fate was effectively sealed. Out of favour with his latest manager, the Turkish international later revealed to beIN Sports Turkey that he felt insignificant under Valverde, having failed to play a single minute during his tenure.

In a recent development, he subsequently left Barcelona on loan to return to Turkey with Istanbul Basaksehir, before making a permanent return to Galatasaray in 2020. He retired just two years later, aged 35, bringing the curtain down on a career that had promised so much. His Barcelona spell ultimately yielded just 15 goals and 11 assists in 55 appearances across five years.

Now, however, Turan is embarking on a new chapter in football, having swapped the pitch for the dugout and taken charge of Shakhtar Donetsk in 2025.

There are no better examples of Turan's downward spiral than the fact he was given two separate prison sentences in the latter stages of his career.

In 2018, Turan became embroiled in a nightclub altercation that left Turkish pop star Berkay Sahin with a broken nose. According to Sahin's wife, Ozlem Ada Sahin, the former Barcelona midfielder had made inappropriate advances towards her before turning on her husband.

It has been revealed that in an even more bizarre twist, Turan later arrived at the hospital where Berkay was undergoing surgery, armed with a gun. He reportedly begged the singer for forgiveness, even telling him to shoot him if he genuinely believed he had harassed his wife.

The incident ultimately landed Turan with a suspended prison sentence of two years and eight months for firing a gun with the intention of causing panic, illegally possessing firearms and intentionally injuring someone, as reported by BBC News.

His second sentence came in March 2024 when he was slapped with a one-year suspended prison sentence and fined roughly €630,000 by a Spanish court after pleading guilty to two counts of tax fraud covering the 2015 and 2016 tax years during his time with Barcelona.

Industry News: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion.
  • It has been revealed that "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related problems and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was introduced.

It has been revealed that "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related problems and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their concern is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club remarked "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

In a recent development, this campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (SUBSTANTIAL) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

Industry observers note that the fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's proposal" and that homosexuality is a sin.

According to recent reports, borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

Recent findings suggest that the use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Massive-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

And yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the newly introduced opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

“The one thing that will happen under my ownership is that whenever we enter the transfer market, we will play to win. That’s the theme I set out at the start of this year. So if we make a move in any window, January or June, it will be a move that counts.”.

Such hopes quickly evaporated after eight minutes when Leny Yoro received a red card for bringing Alexander Isak down, although whether his sending off was justified is up for debate.

What isn't up for debate is the capitulation from Pochettino's men as Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the free-kick Isak won. Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 before goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz in the second half handed the Red Devils their fifth league defeat of the season.

United's defeat is the worst a new manager has suffered in 100 years, another nightmare record in a season of history being made by the club for all the wrong reasons. Sitting 19th just over a week before December means the possibility of Pochettino's side spending the campaign fighting relegation is becoming increasingly likely.

Sources indicate that mainoo has been one of the very few positives at Old Trafford this season and the young English midfielder firmly believes Yoro's sending off is responsible for the loss on Merseyside. He spoke to Sky Sports after the game and made his stance clear over the red card:.

"This doesn't define us, you know? I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.".

According to recent reports, he added: "But we have to come together because the games are coming thick and fast. We can't dwell on it too long, but we have to take the pain and use it to bring us together.".

Upcoming United boss Pochettino hit out at Sam Barrott's decision to send Yoro off and compared the challenge to Jeremy Jacquet's on Bryan Mbeumo just minutes prior. And Mainoo agreed with his coach's verdict:.

"No chance. The ball's already with the keeper, they're both running full speed, what can he do? But it is what it is. It's 10 vs 11. When you come to a place like Anfield it's already a tough game. You lose a man and it makes it hard. But I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game right until the end. We just have to take the pain and move on with it.".

It has been revealed that united's problems extend further than a defeat to rivals Liverpool and Yoro's sending off means he'll miss Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday. After shipping four at Anfield, they have now conceded more goals (34) than any club across Europe's top five leagues and have just eight points from 11 league games.

Some rival fans have interpreted Mainoo to be considering the defeat to Liverpool an anomaly and were quick to point out United's results so far this season. With just one win in 11 top-flight games, many disagree that this game doesn't define Pochettino's strugglers.

A Liverpool fan responded: "When City went down to 10 men early against Utd away, they conceded just 0.8 xG for the rest of the game. United conceded 4.6 xG today.".

Another member of the Kop fanbase added: "Brother you've only won a single game since the league started in August we're almost hitting December.".

One supporter agreed with this take: "Course it doesn't define ya, being 19th after 11 games does lil Bro.".

Even an Aston Villa fan weighed in: "Talking like it’s a one off, what about the other 15 games you’ve played this season.".

A United supporter also took issue with Mainoo's comments: "Bro do your talking on the pitch. Too many of these players have fat lot to say outside of the pitch but nothing to show on it.".

In a recent development, that last response sums up how United fans have felt throughout the disastrous start to the season. Many of the players who are letting their team down have chosen to either air their grievances publicly or send out repetitive apologetic social media posts.

Sources indicate that it's hard not to sympathise with Mainoo, who is playing for his boyhood club and only wants to see them battle their way out of such a precarious situation. He unfortunately finds himself in a squad that CEO Omar Berrada feels has improved since the summer, but sitting 19th in the league with Christmas on the horizon surely suggests otherwise.

Chelsea, however, offer the more immediate pathway.

The Reds then doubled their lead just a few moments later, with Ngumoha finding Florian Wirtz in the box, who produced a phenomenal finish to make it 2-0 on 13 minutes.

Liverpool made it 3-0 after 66 minutes as Ngumoha finally got himself on the scoresheet.

It was a game that summed up many of United's problems, particularly defensively, and it certainly demonstrated Mauricio Pochettino that he's got his work cut out.

Ngumoha in particular was incredibly impressive, and it sums up United's problems that he was a player the Red Devils were hoping to get.

He certainly wouldn't solve all of United's problems, considering they desperately need defensive reinforcements, but it's a real kick in the teeth for the youngster to tear them apart at Anfield.

United had an experienced right-back in Dalot. Going head-to-head with him, but the Portuguese defender certainly lost that battle.

This is likely to continue being a common theme for United going forward, considering their current position in the Premier League table.

The Red Devils sit in 19th position, having won just once this season, and are in real danger of getting relegated unless Pochettino can turn things around rapidly.

As a result, United are going to find it incredibly difficult to attract players, just like they did with Ngumoha.

In the past, United have always been able to attract players due to the stature of the club, but their league position is going to carry a lot of weight going forward.

The Red Devils are going to fall further and further behind as players such as Ngumoha choose other clubs.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

In a recent development, the team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a big decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating substantial chances.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with newly introduced manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United demonstrates just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller tech giant she worked for.

According to recent reports, alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing tech giant. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

According to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the company advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed says it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

This type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

At the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the company's website as of November 2026.

According to recent reports, "There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate manufacturer," it mentioned. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the New York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

According to recent reports, megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the organization's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

It has been revealed that alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

In December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the company was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell company with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

According to recent reports, this was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

According to recent reports, this was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

Recent findings suggest that “I have to take the responsibility,” he remarked. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the plan. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

According to recent reports, “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the initiative disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it shows.”.

According to recent reports, newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

If they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Industry observers note that concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight latest signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat quickly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

Sources indicate that there was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

According to recent reports, everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game proposal, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

According to recent reports, A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

According to recent reports, the groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

It has been revealed that this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

Industry observers note that it was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

Recent findings suggest that he did not follow those blunt instructions. Everton took the lead in such simple fashion and all Jaissle and his coaching staff could do was shake their heads at each other. Tyrique George was played in far too easily from a free-kick but his shot should have been saved by Hornicek. It was straight at the Czech, but it went through him and it left Barry with a tap in. Newcastle appealed for both a foul on Fabian Schar and an offside but got neither.

This was going to be a younger, more dynamic squad that would grow with the club as they looked to live up to the promise made by David Hopkinson, the chief executive, that they would be “consistently and credibly challenging” for top honours in England and Europe by 2030.

In a recent development, newcastle are 12th in the Premier League, but have had an inconsistent start and there are concerns that too many of these signings have failed to shine. Jaissle is leaning heavily on the players he inherited from Howe instead.

Despite the heavy away defeats and unconvincing performances, that would be an impressive start for a fresh manager. Matthias Jaissle has already felt the full force of the contrasting emotions on Tyneside in his three months in charge but significant questions hang over his team. Virgil van Dijk and David Raya are now two of the best players in the Premier League, accumulating 528 English top-flight appearances between them. Naturally, this means that the pair have played alongside some of the very best in the game.

Van Dijk made a name for himself in British football at Celtic and Southampton, before completing his significant move to Liverpool. At Anfield, he's established himself as one of the greatest defenders in Premier League history, whilst winning two league titles and a Champions League in the process.

Meanwhile, Raya doesn't quite have the longevity at the top level as his Dutch counterpart, but he has developed into one of the world's best goalkeepers since signing for Arsenal in 2023.
