According to recent reports, while the pair have had the pleasure of sharing dressing rooms with an array of world-class players, they've also played alongside several players who didn't quite reach the outstanding level that they did. Former Celtic number nine Anthony Stokes falls into that category.

Eight years after leaving Celtic, Stokes was sentenced to 15 months in prison.

Born in Dublin, Stokes joined Arsenal's academy at the age of 15. After developing through the Gunners' youth system, Stokes left the North London club after making just a single appearance for the first team.

Sources indicate that he'd go on to have stints at Sunderland and Hibernian, before making his way to Celtic, where he enjoyed the most fruitful spell of his career. Netting 76 goals in 191 appearances for the Scottish giants, he then left Glasgow and spent the last six years of his career jumping from club to club, spending time in Greece, Azerbaijan, Turkey and Iran.

Sources indicate that three years after hanging up his boots, Stokes was arrested and found guilty of drug and driving offences. However, he successfully won an appeal against the verdict, and the sentence was eventually overturned.

It has been revealed that A prolific striker in his youth career at Arsenal, Arsene Wenger started to take note of Stokes heading into the 2005/06 season. In October 2005, the Frenchman called the then 17-year-old up to the Gunners' matchday squad for a League Cup tie against Sunderland.

Sources indicate that wenger handed Stokes his senior debut that day, introducing the Irishman in the 88th minute in place of Arturo Lupoli, with the North Londoners running out 3-0 winners. While this proved to be his one and only appearance for the Premier League giants' first team, it wasn't yet the end of him at Arsenal.

To aid his development by playing regular minutes, Wenger sent Stokes out to Falkirk on loan in 2006. The forward enjoyed a prolific stint at the Scottish club, scoring 16 goals in 18 appearances, prompting praise from the legendary Gunners coach upon his return to North London.

"Anthony has made a major step up to the SPL and has done very well - I'm very happy about it. Ideally, I'd like all of our young kids on loan to come back to Arsenal." - Wenger on Stokes in 2006 (via BBC Sport).

Despite Wenger's words, there was no room for Stokes at Arsenal. He joined Sunderland in January 2007 for £2 million, and after struggling to make an impact at the Stadium of Light, he eventually made his way back to Scotland in 2009, signing for Hibernian.

Industry observers note that lighting up the Scottish Premiership again, scoring 23 goals in his solitary season at Hibs, Celtic came in and acquired the striker in August 2010. Signing a four-year contract in Glasgow, Stokes rapidly established himself as a fan favourite at Celtic Park.

In a recent development, he enjoyed two seasons where he surpassed the 20-goal mark, and ultimately left the Bhoys with four Premiership winners' medals in his back pocket. This spell with the Hoops is where he met Van Dijk, whom he shared a dressing room with between 2013 and 2015, before the centre-back signed for Southampton.

After a loan spell back in Edinburgh with Hibs, Stokes briefly returned to English football, leaving Celtic for Blackburn Rovers in 2016. His stint in Lancashire wasn't very successful, making just 14 appearances for the Blues and Whites, although he did cross paths with future Yashin Trophy nominee Raya at Ewood Park.

According to recent reports, stokes then spiralled into a classic 'journeyman' path as he entered the latter stages of his career. He returned to Hibs for a third time, before playing for Apollon Smyrnis, Tractor, Adana Demirspor, Persepolis and Livingston, all in the space of four years.

Many thought his spell at Livingston would be his final, but Stokes returned to the game in August 2025, five years after last playing, signing for Conor McGregor's pub team, Black Forge.

Recent findings suggest that stokes had a history of criminal convictions before he was finally sentenced to prison in 2024. In 2013, the striker was convicted of assault after headbutting park attendant Anthony Bradley in a Dublin nightclub.

It has been revealed that in 2019, he pleaded guilty to stalking his ex-girlfriend and her mother in Scotland. He spent short periods in prison for each of these offences before he was handed a 15-month sentence in 2024.

Sources indicate that the former professional footballer was caught following a high-speed car chase in Dublin and was reportedly found guilty of possessing £3,300 worth of cocaine in the process. Stokes was deemed to be over the alcohol limit and driving at 99mph when he nearly collided with another motorist in early January 2023.

He also entered an additional guilty plea to possessing 86 illegal street tablets in Dublin, ten days after the traffic pursuit.

It has been revealed that alongside his 15-month sentence, Stokes was banned from driving for five years. However, he was released within hours in order to appeal the severity of the sentence. In November 2024, his sentence was overturned on appeal, meaning he successfully evaded jail time.

Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception.
  • But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is key to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

"I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

It has been revealed that although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

The match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

It has been revealed that at some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

In a recent development, for now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.
  • Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

According to recent reports, such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification at the moment. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

We could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Recent findings suggest that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

Sources indicate that we wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their fresh ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Industry observers note that palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Industry observers note that colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are right now in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Sources indicate that since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

#71502. Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious.
  • But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.
  • Industry observers note that this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men.".

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.

Industry observers note that this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

Recent findings suggest that "I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposedly be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a upcoming exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.

It has been revealed that the exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust. Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

In a recent development, in the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing fresh or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people.".

According to recent reports, european colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met. Forced labor was also central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.

While racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski states the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

Industry observers note that "In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," indicates Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued.".

On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

Sources indicate that one area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.

The glitch of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

The mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator said what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.

Martinican intellectual Aime Cesaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

Industry observers note that germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance. However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi noted. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten games into the 2026/27 Premier League season and it is fair to say that Tottenham are lacking a little bit in firepower.

Spurs went the first four games of the campaign without scoring and are among the lowest scorers in the league now, with only Sunderland and Nottingham Forest having scored fewer.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the club's top scorer in the Premier League with two goals, with seven players on one goal each.

GIVEMESPORT understands that Tottenham will enter the January transfer window looking for a striker, with senior football correspondent Ben Jacobs saying in September: "Tottenham are prepared to add another striker mid-season in the winter market if goals continue to dry up.".

Eli Junior Kroupi is a name who has been linked with a move to N17, with Spurs holding an interest in him in the summer transfer window before he picked up an injury that kept him out of action for the first few months of the season.

Industry observers note that he is back for Bournemouth now, but will command a hefty fee, with the Cherries reluctant to sell mid-season. Igor Matanovic at Freiburg is another name that has been tipped for a move to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, but Jacobs added in his most recent GMS newsletter that he was "unlikely to be available in the winter market".

With Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush on one goal apiece and Richarlison left out of the club's Premier League squad altogether, Spurs are in need of firepower if they are to continue their charge up the table. And there is one player that nobody is talking about who could just be Spurs' next Harry Kane.

In a recent development, replacing someone of Kane's stature is no mean feat, given he has just won the Ballon d'Or with Bayern Munich to become one of the oldest Ballon d'Or winners. Richarlison, Solanke and now Marmoush have tried to live up to those lofty expectations and it would be unfair to even expect them to get anywhere close to Kane's standards. He is the club's all-time top scorer, after all.

The 26-year-old is 6ft 1ins, one inch shorter than Kane, and has something of a similar path in football to the England captain. Sinayoko has paid his dues in the lower leagues in France, as Kane did in loan spells with the likes of Norwich City, Leyton Orient, Millwall and Leicester City, before making his mark in Ligue Un.

Industry observers note that kane became a revelation in the Premier League at the age of 21, scoring 21 goals in 34 games for Spurs in 2014/15 - Mauricio Pochettino's first season in charge - on his way to becoming one of the greatest Premier League players of all time. Sinayoko started to make his mark aged 23 in 2023/24, scoring nine and assisting five in 35 appearances for Ligue 2 side Auxerre.

Sources indicate that the same number of goal contributions followed in 24/25, albeit with five goals and nine assists this time. But that was after a step up to Ligue Un following Auxerre's promotion.

It has been revealed that last season Sinayoko bagged 12 goals and four assists in 32 games, but, aged 26 now, he has shown he is well and truly up to speed in one of Europe's significant five leagues. He already has nine goals and five assists in 10 appearances for Paris FC, having made the move in the summer transfer window.

He is the joint third top scorer in Europe's top five leagues this season with nine in the league, the same number as Manchester City star Erling Haaland.

It has been revealed that sinayoko's all-round ability, to score goals and create them, makes him comparable, to a much lesser extent of course, to Kane, while his career trajectory from lower league to the very top, perhaps slightly slower than those who make the grade as teenagers, is also similar. He can also play as a support striker or off the two wings.

Sinayoko is not a name on many people's lips at the moment, but if he carries on his top form, his star will rise. He is unproven in one of the bigger domestic leagues, and that would be a risk for Spurs, but he clearly knows where the goal is and that is what Roberto De Zerbi and Spurs are primarily missing right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI (or, GTA VI) has finally arrived after 13 years of waiting, and Italian football has joined in on the hype, from the newspaper front pages to the coaches’ press conferences.

Industry observers note that as noted by Il Fatto Quotidiano, the game released at midnight on 19 November. Football quickly caught on. Milan, Inter, Juventus and Lazio all marked the release on social media, Corriere dello Sport turned its Sunday front page into a GTA tribute, and two of Italy’s best-known coaches were asked whether their players would be up all night with a controller in their hands.

Industry observers note that corriere dello Sport’s Sunday front page was the standout. “GTA ttuso 32” was how the paper opened the day after Gattuso’s win over Lecce, playing on the Lazio coach’s name. The 32 refers to Lazio’s points tally, with the Biancocelesti top on their own, “+2 on Gasp and +4 on Chivu”.

Sources indicate that lazio’s 3-0 win was summed up as “Divertimento Lazio”, and “Meraviglia Noslin” was drawn in the style of the video game everyone has been talking about for days. Tijjani Noslin is the main figure in the illustration, with Davide Frattesi and Gattuso embracing behind him.

Milan posted a carousel that turns their players into characters inspired by the look of Grand Theft Auto, captioned “The characters we want in GTA VI”. One image demonstrated Adrien Rabiot driving through Vice City, and another had Strahinja Pavlović at a petrol station. The Rossoneri followed up with “Growing up takes time. So did GTA VI”, a nod to the 13 years since GTA V.

Inter went for a debate instead. Curtis Jones and Djed Spence discussed the series on the way to training: Jones named San Andreas and GTA V as his favourites, while Spence went for Vice City. Juventus, meanwhile, used the game’s graphic style to present Kenan Yildiz and some of his teammates.

According to recent reports, if the social media teams were excited, Gattuso clearly wasn’t. Asked in his pre-match press conference before Lecce whether the game might distract his players, the Lazio coach seemed to have no idea what it was.

“I don’t even know what you’re talking about. Is it a video game? I didn’t know. With that name, I thought it was a car,” he mentioned.

“If they play at night, that’s their business. I’m not going to start checking up on them.

Industry observers note that “This job requires self-respect. At breakfast together, I’ll try to work out if anyone has been staying up late.”.

Asked about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, who had remarked he would be playing the game after training, Gattuso added: “That’s part of being a professional and caring about your job. I would never tell an individual player not to play.”.

Despite all that, Gattuso still ended up in the world of Vice City in a video published by Lazio.

Roberto De Zerbi was more direct. The Tottenham coach was asked the same question at his pre-match press conference before facing Ipswich Town.

“Listen, I am not a policeman, I am not a father, I am a coach,” he said. “I think in my dressing room are good people, mature people, so the PlayStation or other things, the right time they can close, but otherwise I go in their room and I destroy the GTA and the other things.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have taken an crucial step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister’s long-term future, with the Argentina international eager to extend his stay at Anfield.

The 27-year-old had previously been disappointed after being told that a renewal was not immediately planned, but his excellent form this season appears to have changed the club’s thinking.

With Real Madrid also monitoring his situation, Liverpool now have good reason to resolve the matter before uncertainty grows.

According to Football Insider, Liverpool have opened preliminary discussions with Mac Allister’s representatives over a new contract.

His current deal runs until 2028, but the midfielder is understood to be extremely keen to extend his stay.

That represents a significant change from earlier in the season, when Mac Allister admitted he had been hurt by Liverpool’s previous decision not to prioritise a renewal.

His performances have strengthened his case considerably. Mac Allister has scored five goals already this season and has re-established himself as one of Andoni Iraola’s most crucial midfielders.

Liverpool’s decision also comes amid continued interest from Real Madrid, who explored a possible deal earlier this year.

There is little reason for Liverpool to allow this situation to drift.

A CaughtOffside report confirmed through Fabrizio Romano that talks have started, while also revealing Real Madrid explored signing Mac Allister towards the end of May.

That interest should sharpen Liverpool’s focus.

Mac Allister is entering his prime, understands the Premier League and offers a rare combination of creativity, intelligence and defensive discipline. Replacing him with a player of similar quality would likely cost considerably more than improving his current terms.

Liverpool have already seen Trent Alexander-Arnold leave for Real Madrid, so allowing another vital player to move closer to the final year of his contract would create unnecessary risk.

Industry observers note that the player’s stance also makes negotiations easier. Mac Allister wants to remain at Anfield, meaning Liverpool are not trying to convince an unhappy player to stay. They simply need to show that his importance is reflected in the contract they offer.

If both sides genuinely want the same outcome, this should be one of Liverpool’s simplest major decisions of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An all-smiles Mauricio Pochettino took his seat in the dugout at Anfield, and just eight minutes after kick-off, he wore a face of despair and realised this Manchester United team have a mountain to climb.

Industry observers note that any hope of a latest manager bounce coming into effect for United was rapidly extinguished by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending off, followed almost immediately by Dominik Szoboszlai's 10th-minute free-kick. Down to ten men, his side conceded a second three minutes later when Florian Wirtz found the back of Senne Lammens' net.

Industry observers note that rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled more misery on the Red Devils, whose new coach has been thrown back into Premier League management in the midst of a crisis. He made some bold decisions heading into today's game against Liverpool, and they played their part in a fifth league defeat of the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that as soon as United released Pochettino's first lineup since his appointment, eyebrows were raised, and Sky Sports' Gary Neville admitted that he'd already conceded defeat upon seeing Matthijs de Ligt chosen in defence. That's not because of the Dutch defender's ability, but rather his lack of football over the past 10 months, having struggled on his return in a 4-1 defeat to Como at the end of October.

According to recent reports, de Ligt seems to be shaking off the rust, and starting him at Anfield didn't pan out as Pochettino envisioned. He was largely at fault for Yoro's dismissal, caught way too high up the pitch, allowing Alexander Isak to pounce, burst forward, and buy the foul from De Ligt's defensive partner.

Recent findings suggest that the 27-year-old has endured an injury-ridden spell since joining the club from Bayern Munich in August 2024. A sluggish outing against Liverpool raises question marks over Pochettino's understanding of his squad, especially when picking him over Harry Maguire.

Industry observers note that another head-scratching decision Pochettino made was to start Patrick Dorgu on the left wing. Bryan Mbeumo started over on the right and Matheus Cunha played through the middle, albeit for just 22 minutes before Maguire came on for Mbeumo.

Like De Ligt, Dorgu has similarly been working his way back to full fitness recently after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The Dane is a versatile option, spending the majority of Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back tenure as a left wing-back.

In a recent development, that's not to say Dorgu hasn't impressed occasionally over the course of his United career, and he was probably one of the few positives today. Still, prioritising him over Mbeumo, who scored in this fixture last season, and Cunha, whom Pochettino brought off for Joshua Zirkzee, was rather puzzling.

As was the omission of Shea Lacey, who has been catching the eye every time he's been afforded an opportunity. The English wonderkid can surely do no more, yet even with Amad struggling and benched, he seemingly finds himself third in the pecking order.

This brings us onto Pochettino's substitutions, which caused a stir online, especially the decision to hook Cunha for Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian has been a saviour in the past, most recently coming to the rescue in a 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma.

Industry observers note that cunha indicated unbelievable passion that night, even refusing to leave the pitch after receiving a second yellow card for taking his shirt off while celebrating his winner. Of the attackers available to Pochettino right now, he's the one who can make something happen out of nothing.

Mbeumo fell victim to Yoro's sending off, with his new coach forced to bring Maguire on to address the one-man disadvantage. It's difficult to assess whether he'd have had much influence once Liverpool went two-nil ahead, but he's another forward who can come alive when the going gets tough.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino needs more time with his squad, and decisions such as starting De Ligt over Maguire are clear evidence of this. It's worth pointing out that the Argentine arrived at Carrington on Wednesday, four days prior to the trip to Anfield, and took his first training session on Thursday.

It has been revealed that before that, he took charge of two final games as the United States national team manager, overseeing wins over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals. This isn't so much Pochettino's fault, but for a club sitting 19th and in such a turbulent situation, having him introduced to his squad just four days before a clash with Liverpool is alarming.

United confirmed they came to an agreement with the USMNT for Pochettino to see out his role during the international break, during which only 13 of their 33-man squad were called up. Their official confirmation of his appointment came on November 13th, nine days ago, with the club already languishing in 19th place.

According to recent reports, had they turned to an available coach such as Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte, they surely would have been in the building as soon as the contract was signed. It's a damning example of everything wrong at the club that co-owners INEOS didn't feel it necessary to get Pochettino into Manchester as soon as possible to at least start planning before such a crucial game.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.
  • In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.
  • It has been revealed that still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," stated Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.

In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.

It has been revealed that still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," stated Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement. Denmark is leading the way across all four categories assessed — energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and national climate policy. A total of 15 states, including Lithuania, Chile, and Morocco, received an overall "high" rating, which is two more than last year.

The European Union also moved up a spot, while Hungary jumped 21 places after the ousting of former prime minister Viktor Orban's government, which had repeatedly vetoed EU climate plans, dismissing them as a "utopian fantasy.".

The top three positions on the CCPI remained vacant again this year, as no country has yet done enough to meet global climate goals aimed at preventing worsening weather extremes and climate damage.

In a recent development, "We are seeing a striking contrast," stated Burck. "Progress on climate action is often slow and in some countries, such as the United States, things are even moving backwards. But technologically and economically there is enormous momentum.".

That momentum is apparent in record solar energy growth. Last year 75% of global electricity demand growth was met by the green energy source, according to energy think tank Ember's latest global electricity review. Investment in clean energy has also outpaced that in fossil fuels for multiple years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rapid expansion of renewable technology, as well as the Iran War and a reduction in deforestation are behind a projected slight fall in emissions for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the CCPI.

"Governments have to act now to turn the momentum into sustained emissions reductions," said CCPI co-author Niklas Höhne of the NewClimate Institute, which compiles the report with environmental NGO Germanwatch.

Burck attributed Germany's worst ever performance in the category of national climate policy to current policies being pursued by Germany's economy minister Katherina Reiche.

"Measures that primarily aim to increase the use of natural gas, threaten to undermine progress in the energy transition and risk significantly worsening the conditions for renewable energy and electrification for many years to come," noted Burck.

A European Commission report published on November 9 on the sidelines of the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey stated Germany was one of nine EU countries set to miss 2030 emissions reductions targets.

Germany is not alone in its disappointing ranking. The other G20 countries — the world's leading industrialized and emerging economies, responsible for around 80% of global CO2 emissions — also perform poorly.

The only exception among them is the United Kingdom, which ranks seventh and received a high rating, performing well in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and climate policy. However, study authors rated it low for renewable energy expansion.

Sources indicate that the G20's oil- and gas-producing countries occupy some of the lowest positions on the climate action table. The United States, which is the world's second largest emitter, languishes alongside Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Canada around the bottom of the league, with an overall rating of "very low.".

It has been revealed that the hosts of this year's COP31, also received a "low" overall score. Australia, a major coal exporter with some of the world's highest per-capita emissions, ranks 54th, while Turkey, which is also heavily dependent on fossil fuels, comes in 53rd.

China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases and ranks 56th in the CCPI, receiving an overall rating of "very low." Its main weaknesses include its now high per-capita emissions and substantial energy consumption.

However, among the G20, China leads the way in renewable energy expansion. The country, which is five years ahead of schedule in reaching its goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030, also produces over 80% of the world's solar panels.

Several oil-producing countries, including Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates, are also performing better than expected in the renewables category and "are significantly expanding their previously limited" capacity, stated the report.

The authors mentioned these countries have significant potential to further expand renewables.

Sources indicate that "In the Arab states in particular, very high per-capita emissions and an above-average level of electrification coincide with a relatively low existing share of renewable energy and enormous solar potential," said co-author Natalie Pelekh in a statement. "These are, in fact, ideal conditions for more ambitious climate action.".

This article was originally published in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

In a recent development, fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, notes Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two new studies. “This is a really massive deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The company also launched their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has announced aims to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Sources indicate that roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

But when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

It has been revealed that amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she said: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

According to recent reports, artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most notable value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

Do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, says public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

In the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

According to recent reports, vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

According to recent reports, today I’m considering buying a prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) in case of a power cut. Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the newly introduced head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Recent findings suggest that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

The players learned for the first time that Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr were leaving camp, and they headed straight to Manchester.

#71490. DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (943 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (943 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black?
  • Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?
  • Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know when you lock your phone and the screen goes black? It seems like it's not doing anything. But it's not doing nothing. It's syncing your messages, updating apps and running other background processes.

Your brain has its own version of that.

Imagine you're sitting on a bus, staring out of a window, taking a shower or walking, and you get that feeling of doing nothing and letting your mind drift?

Well, your mind, the brain, is doing a lot when it feels like you're doing nothing.

It's going over your memories, shaping your sense of who you are, imagining possible futures, helping you understand other people and connecting ideas.

That's your brain's default mode network.

Scientists conducted brain-imaging experiments in the 1990s and early 2000s to find out which regions of the brain were active during demanding tasks, like solving a math problem or memory exercise.

But to measure that, they needed a so-called baseline. They needed to know the level of brain activity at rest and during demanding tasks.

So, between the tasks, they asked participants to relax, close their eyes, stare at a fixed point on a wall, or try not to think of anything at all.

And they measured the participants' brain activity both when they were solving a task and doing nothing. That's how scientists noticed the brain was active in up- and downtime.

They noticed that when participants started to focus on a newly introduced task, after having done nothing, some brain areas lit up and other areas dimmed down. That suggests those areas that dimmed down must have been active while the participant was apparently — physically and mentally — at rest.

This realization eventually led to the discovery of the default mode network or DMN.

The DMN is crucial because it helps your brain make sense of your life and experiences.

It helps you connect and revisit memories, reflect on who you are, imagine what might happen in future scenarios, understand other people, build meaning from experience, and connect ideas in newly introduced ways.

Industry observers note that it turns all your memories, experiences, knowledge, emotions and social information into your internal story. Think of that story as a constantly evolving, updated model of who you are and how you engage with the world around you.

According to recent reports, but it's important to understand the DMN involves more than one area of the brain. It is a group of brain regions that light up when you're not focused on an external task.

In a recent development, there's another player in your brain that acts as a monitoring system. You can think of it as constantly asking "Is there anything that needs my attention?".

Imagine you're daydreaming while driving, and a car suddenly swerves into your lane.

In a fraction of a second, your daydream disappears and your attention snaps back to the road. That player is called the salience network, or SN.

The salience network helps you notice important signals, like a sound, a mistake, pain, an emotion, a threat, or something happening in your body, and helps shift the brain toward attention and control systems when action is needed.

The DMN, SN and attention/control systems constantly interact.

In a recent development, and the DMN doesn't just turn off completely with every hard task. Parts of it can also contribute when tasks involve memory, stories, meaning or other people.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Smartphones have filled many of the small empty moments of our days — waiting for the bus, standing in line, eating alone, lying on the couch. We are constantly looking at our devices.

So, it seems reasonable to ask: are we crowding out those moments of boredom where DMN kicks in?

Maybe. But so far, there's no strong evidence that scrolling directly affects mental health by reducing DMN time.

What we do know is that problematic smartphone use can increase stress, anxiety, task-switching and disrupt sleep.

And sleep loss and stress also have clearer evidence for altering DMN-related brain connectivity.

The DMN is not always necessarily good.

When your mind wanders, it might produce a great new idea.

But it might also replay an embarrassing thing you did five years ago. Again. And again.

In depression, the self-reflection part of the DMN can get caught in repetitive negative loops that are hard to stop — what's known as rumination.

Sources indicate that scientists have also found that Alzheimer's disease targets key DMN areas, particularly those responsible for your autobiographical memory and remembering other aspects of the past. Which may help explain why memory problems are so central to the disease.

According to recent reports, protect your sleep and take stress seriously. There is direct evidence that sleep loss and stress disrupt DMN-related connectivity.

It has been revealed that take real, quiet breaks after mentally demanding tasks, like studying. It can even help you memorize facts for your exam.

Embrace boredom and enjoy doing nothing.

Try to reframe boredom as this essential, energy-intensive active work in your brain that builds your internal narrative and sense of self, consolidates memories, creates connections and sparks creativity.

In a recent development, try waiting in line without checking your phone. Look out the window next time you take the bus or take a walk without listening to anything.

Sources indicate that you can also try scheduling DMN time. It may be the closest thing to a real brain hack.

Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of Manchester United ended in a disappointing 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that looking to get off to the best possible start, Pochettino's United tenure couldn't have begun much worse. Indeed, the Reds were reduced to ten men in the eighth minute after Leny Yoro was sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

According to recent reports, A long ball over the top of the United back-line caused havoc, and after Matthias de Ligt misread the flight of the ball, Alexander Isak ran through on goal, only for Yoro to bring him down outside the box. As Isak was about to shoot and have a chance at scoring, Yoro hauled him to the floor, and referee Sam Barrott had no choice but to brandish the red card.

In a recent development, from the resulting free-kick, Liverpool went 1-0 up. Dominik Szoboszlai fired the ball through the crowd and into the bottom corner, giving Senne Lammens no chance and sending the Anfield crowd into delirium.

In a recent development, three minutes later, Liverpool doubled their lead. Rio Ngumoha dribbled past Diogo Dalot with ease before squaring the ball across the face for Florian Wirtz to volley home from close-range.

Liverpool created a number of big chances to extend their lead further, but had to wait until the 66th minute to make it 3-0. Blistering pace from Bradley Barcola saw him steam clear of Lisandro Martinez before squaring for Ngumoha to tap home.

Sources indicate that it proved to be another frustrating and difficult evening at the office for Dalot, who let Pochettino down with a dismal performance against Liverpool. Ngumoha - and then Victor Munoz - had so much joy against the Portuguese on Liverpool's left.

Dalot should have done so much better with his defending in the lead-up to Liverpool's second goal. He allowed Ngumoha to have too much space to glide past him on the outside and therefore couldn't get back to block the cross, which led to Wirtz scoring.

Industry observers note that throughout, Dalot couldn't handle Ngumoha. He wasn't able to deal with his pace and threat both on the inside and outside, and even when United defended in a compact shape, he was caught out of position time and time again.

When United pushed to pull one back in the second half, Dalot got caught high up the pitch leading to Liverpool's third goal. His man, Ngumoha, was free in aces of space at the far post and had the simplest of tasks to slot home.

Even after Ngumoha was taken off in the 78th minute, Dalot's evening didn't get much easier. Munoz moved out to the left and was effective against the out-of-form United defender, playing a one-two with Wirtz inside the channel before scoring.

Recent findings suggest that overall, Dalot was given a dire 5.3 rating by Flashscore, the lowest out of any United player on the pitch. He won just TWO out of his 11 duels, won just two tackles, committed two fouls and was dribbled past twice.

In a recent development, yoro and De Ligt weren't good, but Dalot was even worse, and he should be taken out of the firing line by Pochettino going into Wednesday's Champions League trip to Sporting CP. Noussair Mazraoui should instead start at right-back.

According to recent reports, celta Vigo were rarely troubled in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Friday 13 November. Jutglà struck twice before the half-hour mark, and Swedberg added a late double after Salamanca UDS had gone down to ten men.

The Galician side were 3-0 up at the break at Villares de la Reina. They finished with goals from three different players and assists from five team-mates, against a Salamanca side coached by Jorge García.

Jutglà opened the scoring in the 15th minute, converting an assist from Milla. Eight minutes later he struck again, this time set up by Febas, to put Celta firmly in control.

Antañón made it three in the 39th minute from an Arcos assist. The tie was effectively settled before the interval.

Salamanca’s evening grew harder after the restart. Murua was booked in the 54th minute, and Levrand was shown a straight red card in the 61st minute, leaving the hosts a man short for the final half-hour.

Celta’s only caution came when Lago was booked in the 72nd minute. The visitors then took advantage of the extra man late on. Swedberg scored in the 80th minute from an Aspas assist and struck again in the 82nd, with Galán providing the pass.

Opara was also booked for Salamanca in the 89th minute as the hosts saw out the closing stages.

Recent findings suggest that the result echoes the previous meeting between the clubs in this competition. Celta won 7-0 in Salamanca on 3 December 2024.

5 goles para selar o pase á seguinte rolda 🔥#UDSCelta ⋄ #CopaDelRey pic.twitter.com/v5Kqou8U4w.

It has been revealed that the win is Celta’s first in any competition since their 2-1 victory over Celtic. In between, they drew 0-0 with Real Betis, lost 3-0 to Rayo Vallecano and 2-1 to Union St. Gilloise, and drew 0-0 with Levante.

For Salamanca, the defeat ended a winning run in which they had beaten Gimnástica Segoviana 1-0 and Real Ávila 3-1.

Salamanca return to Segunda División RFEF Group 5 action at home to Albacete II on Wednesday 18 November. Celta face a far tougher assignment in LaLiga, travelling to Real Madrid on Saturday 21 November.

The Predator Elite, instantly recognisable for its fold-over tongue, is reimagined in BAPEâs signature green ABC CAMO with gold stripes, a shark graphic on the lteral, alternating gold logos on the tongues, and ABC CAMO sockliners.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, the F50 Elite features a striking blue-to-pink gradient ABC CAMO upper, shark graphic on the medial, and clear star prints across the surface. Both pairs are showstoppers built to turn heads on and off the pitch.

Accessories complete the set, with an ABC CAMO duffle bag and a BABY MILO shoulder bag rounding out the collection.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next significant thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

Industry observers note that of course, injuries, personal issues and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

In 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

In a recent development, but things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

After making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

Industry observers note that from that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is right now plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

The first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

However, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

But his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

Sources indicate that the Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian is presently imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

But the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

It has been revealed that the Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never demonstrated his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

In a recent development, he enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the big transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

However, Sanches struggled to find his feet in Germany and was soon sent out on loan to Swansea, where he is perhaps best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a substantial-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

The Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

After six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Industry observers note that back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

Recent findings suggest that it seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

After a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

According to recent reports, two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Recent findings suggest that kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is remarked and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope
